records.title: Structural basis of avian-to-human receptor-binding adaptation in H9Ny influenza A virus hemagglutinin.
records.abstract: The receptor-binding specificity of influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) is a major determinant for viral host tropism, enabling interspecies transmission. The molecular determinants for receptor-binding properties of HAs vary among different IAV subtypes. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis on the receptor-binding determinants of IAV subtype H9 HA and found that the receptor-binding characteristics of H9 subtype influenza viruses have exhibited temporal variations over decades. Q226L (hydrophobicity switch) substitution in the 220-loop is the key determinant for H9 subtype HA to acquire human receptor-binding preference. The amino acid residues of the 130-loop greatly affect the binding of HA protein to canonical receptors. Organoid infection models demonstrate that all three representative viral strains could infect human bronchial epithelial organoids. These findings increase our understanding of the molecular determinants of receptor-binding properties of different HA subtypes and call for the surveillance and response to potential influenza outbreaks, or even epidemics/pandemics.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) subtype H9 poses persistent zoonotic spillover risks due to its adaptive receptor-binding capacity, yet the molecular determinants remain incompletely defined. This study systematically characterizes the receptor-binding determinants of H9 hemagglutinin over decades of viral evolution and identifies two critical functional domains: the 220-loop residue Q226L substitution, which serves as the key mutation conferring human receptor-binding preference, and the 130-loop residues that predominantly modulate canonical receptor-binding affinity. Functional assays using human bronchial epithelial organoids further confirm the robust human infection ability of prevalent H9 viral strains. These findings clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying H9 IAV host tropism and adaptive evolution, provide critical theoretical evidence for targeted influenza surveillance and pandemic preparedness against emerging H9 influenza outbreaks.

records.title: From a surgeon's stroke to a third hemisphere-The auxilium architecture for brain restoration and extension.
records.abstract: A surgeon was exercising on a stationary bicycle when he had a large ischemic left middle cerebral artery territory stroke, complicated by hemorrhagic transformation requiring hemicraniectomy and cranioplasty. He developed right-sided spastic hemiplegia and a mixed aphasia. This paper takes that case as its anchor to pose the question: beyond improving residual function, what would it mean to restore cognitive function that was lost so that the person fully returns to their pre-stroke baseline? Existing brain-computer interfaces rely on the person having an intact cortical substrate for intended movement and speech. Here we propose the Auxilium, a brain restoration architecture for the situation where that substrate is no longer present: an extracranial auxiliary brain system, agnostic to its substrate, that connects to a person's residual cortex through whatever input-output technology proves most appropriate, and that supplies, in parallel and in real time, new substrate, whether biological or synthetic. We address an assumption of brain-computer interface development, that throughput is the binding constraint. Linking a kHz brain to MHz digital does not impart the higher clock speed, because the limitation lies not in the port but in the architecture of the entire brain and body imparted by evolution. We posit that the substrate of canonical circuits and their integration areas is essential, and the Auxilium can be understood as restoring both connectivity (linkage between disconnected areas) and computation (information generation capability of a volume of neural tissue). We propose a near-term de-risking pipeline using stereoelectroencephalography during surgical epilepsy evaluation, comparing extracranial modules spanning threshold rules, PID controllers, expert systems, artificial neural networks, neuromorphic devices, and biological specimens, each linked in real time to a participant serving as their own control on naturalistic tasks. If ports alone restore the lost function, the requirement is routing connectivity. If performance improves only when the module supplies its own dynamics, the requirement is computational substrate. We expect the answer to depend on how much tissue was lost, how quickly, and on the individual's reserve, and we treat routing and substrate as endpoints of a continuum to be mapped empirically.

records.title: Gastric microbiome dysbiosis in chronic atrophic gastritis and gastric cancer: evidence beyond Helicobacter pylori.
records.abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a key precancerous condition in the multistep development of gastric cancer (GC), but the risk of malignant progression varies markedly among patients. Although Helicobacter pylori is the best-established trigger of chronic gastritis, glandular atrophy, and intestinal metaplasia, progressive hypochlorhydria, mucosal barrier impairment, and altered local immunity may also reshape the broader gastric microbiota. Apparent H. pylori-negative status should therefore be interpreted cautiously, as it may reflect previous infection, eradication, false-negative testing, low bacterial burden in advanced lesions, true never-infected status, or autoimmune AG. Enrichment of non-H. pylori taxa alone does not prove microbial replacement or H. pylori-independent causation. This review evaluates links between gastric microbiome remodeling and GC risk in CAG, focusing on microbial composition, functional pathways, mucosal immunity, oxidative stress, and epigenetic alterations. Evidence is interpreted according to disease stage, sample source, study design, and causal strength. Cross-sectional studies show stage-associated microbial differences across non-atrophic gastritis (NAG), CAG, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and GC, but cannot establish temporal direction. Mechanistic data from animal, organoid, and cell models remain model-specific, whereas findings from established GC, intratumoral or fecal microbiota, metastasis, prognosis, and immunotherapy mainly reflect tumor-stage biology. Current evidence supports gastric dysbiosis as a plausible marker or context-dependent modifier, rather than an established independent driver. Prospective CAG-stage cohorts, standardized protocols, rigorous H. pylori classification, and direct functional validation are needed for clinical translation.

records.title: Targeting the cGAS-STING axis in Alzheimer's disease: neuroinflammation-centric therapeutic strategies and perspectives.
records.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder traditionally characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles. However, the limited clinical efficacy of Aβ/tau-targeted therapies has redefined neuroinflammation as an active driver of AD pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) axis acts as a central hub connecting aberrant cytosolic nucleic acid sensing particularly mitochondrial DNA leakage induced by Aβ and tau pathologies to chronic innate immune activation. This review comprehensively elucidates the pathogenic mechanisms of the cGAS-STING axis in AD, detailing its cell-type-specific activation in microglia, astrocytes, and neurons, and its downstream propagation via type I interferons, NF-κB, and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, which collectively drive synaptic damage and neuronal loss. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies, including covalent/non-covalent small-molecule inhibitors (e.g., RU.521, H-151, PF-06928215, SN-011), PROTAC degraders, RNA-based therapies, and immunomodulatory natural products/traditional Chinese medicines (e.g., icariin, tetrahydroxy stilbene glucoside, compound danshen dripping pills). Furthermore, we explore clinical translation prospects, emphasizing cerebrospinal fluid cGAMP and exosomal phosphorylated STING as minimally invasive biomarkers, while addressing key hurdles in blood-brain barrier penetration, and off-target risks. Finally, we highlight future directions involving organoid-microfluidic chip models and precision medicine frameworks to facilitate personalized cGAS-STING-targeted immunotherapy for AD.

records.title: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation: molecular mechanisms and exploration of candidate therapeutic pathways.
records.abstract: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM), formerly termed congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation, is a heterogeneous developmental lung disorder characterized by abnormal cystic or adenomatous structures. Its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood and may involve disturbed lung branching morphogenesis, altered epithelial differentiation, imbalanced cell proliferation and apoptosis, focal somatic mutations, and abnormal epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. This comprehensive narrative review discusses molecular findings relevant to CPAM, including Hoxb-5, SOX2, NKX2.1/TTF-1, FGF10, WNT/BMP, EGFR, RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, ACSL5/WNT2B, FABP7, and TGF-β signaling. We distinguish evidence obtained directly from human CPAM tissue-including expression studies and somatic mutation analyses-from findings extrapolated from normal lung development, animal models, and other pulmonary disorders. Recent morphological, immunohistochemical, molecular, and single-cell studies support substantial histological and molecular heterogeneity, while the relationship between specific histological subtypes and precise developmental windows remains provisional. Chromosomal microarray analysis and sequencing may help identify selected genomic abnormalities, but most candidate pathways have not yet been validated as causal or clinically actionable targets. We summarize key evidence gaps and outline priorities for tissue-resolved profiling, functional validation in organoid and developmental models, and cautious assessment of therapeutic feasibility and safety. This review aims to provide a critical framework for interpreting current CPAM molecular evidence and guiding future translational research.

records.title: Inter-organ interaction axes in systemic inflammation: network pathological mechanisms, pharmacological targets, and precision treatment strategies.
records.abstract: Systemic inflammation plays a central role in both acute and chronic pathological states. Acute inflammation is often triggered by infections or trauma, characterized by rapid immune activation low-grade inflammation is closely associated with aging-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases and diabetes. During disease progression, inter-organ communication forms dynamic networks mediated by metabolites, immune factors, and neural signals, further amplifying the inflammatory response. This article focuses on three key inter-organ interaction axes: the gut-liver-brain axis, the adipose-muscle-bone axis, and the heart-kidney-lung axis. It discusses microbiota-driven metabolic neuroinflammation, immune-metabolic imbalance-induced tissue remodeling, and endothelial and microcirculatory damage in the context of multi-organ inflammation. Based on axis-specific molecular targets and spatiotemporal precision, pharmacological strategies are shifting from single-factor interventions to multitarget combination therapies. Meanwhile, innovative technologies such as single-cell multi-omics, spatial omics, artificial intelligence (AI), and organ-on-a-chip are expediting precision medicine approaches for the individualized treatment of systemic inflammation.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Reprogramming Protein Function by Expanding Chemical and Combinatorial Space: Integrating Chemical and Computational Strategies.
records.abstract: Proteins are biological macromolecules that perform critical functions, including catalysis, molecular recognition, and cellular regulation. Natural evolution has generated remarkable protein diversity, leaving vast opportunities for engineered molecular innovation. Protein engineering has evolved from the rational design of proteins over the last few decades to approaches based on directed evolution and computational methods to enhance their properties. Protein engineering is shifting from optimization-based approaches to an integrated approach, which includes rational design, directed evolution, computational and generative modeling, synthetic chemistry, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation. These strategies widen the scope of experimentally accessible chemical and structural toolboxes in proteins without sacrificing the physicochemical constraints, cellular compatibility, evolutionary processes, and experimental validation. Meanwhile, synthetic chemistry is extending the natural abilities of proteins by incorporating noncanonical amino acids, novel cofactors, and modified metal centers and catalytic environments. These technologies enable the creation of artificial enzymes, programmed molecular binders, synthetic receptors, molecular machines, and biomaterials that have functions beyond those of their natural counterparts. This review introduces advances in the protein engineering field, from past methods of modifying proteins to present-day opportunities for generating proteins with artificial intelligence, and explains how the fields of computation, chemistry, and biology are driving the future of programmable proteins.

records.title: Recent advances in fabrication strategies, functional modulation and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels.
records.abstract: Native protein-based hydrogels not only possess all advantages of their denatured analogues such as exceptional biocompatibility and low toxicity, but also retain the intrinsic function of the protein building block. Therefore, they exhibit novel favorable properties including inherent bioactivity and reversible sol-gel transformation behavior. As such, they have emerged as versatile biomaterials widely used in the biomedical field. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to date overview of design strategies, formation mechanisms, and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels. We systematically summarize the key cross-linking strategies for fabricating reversible native protein-based hydrogels, with particular emphasis on how these interactions govern hydrogel formation and their functionality. We highlight recent advances in fabricating these hydrogels through chemical cross-linking, physical cross-linking, metal coordination, fusion protein design, key interface redesign, de novo design, and modular design strategies, which enable precise control over hierarchical architecture, stimuli-responsiveness, and biomechanical properties. Furthermore, we explore the diverse healthcare applications of these hydrogels, with emphasis on drug delivery, wound healing, and tissue engineering. Finally, we discuss perspectives on future directions, including the integration of computational modeling, machine learning, and high-throughput experimentation to enable rational design of smart, multifunctional native protein-based hydrogels with tailored performances for next-generation biomedical applications.

records.title: Natural language-guided generation of molecular structures for single-molecule electronics.
records.abstract: As molecular science advances toward autonomous scientific discovery, enabling AI models to directly generate valid molecular structures from natural language descriptions has emerged as a critical requirement. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the ability to map discrete chemical space into continuous semantic representation for general molecular generation, their application to single-molecule electronics (SME) remains largely unexplored. This is primarily due to the specific topological requirements of the field, such as the necessity of an anchor-backbone-anchor motif for electrode connection. In this work, we propose SingMolT5, a fine-tuned molecular LLM for natural language-guided generation of single molecules. We systematically evaluated the structural generation performance using both in-context learning (ICL) and fine-tuning strategies based on a carefully curated domain-specific instruction-tuning dataset. Results show that while ICL can capture basic molecular syntax, only the fine-tuning model can reliably enforce the anchor-backbone-anchor motif required for single-molecule measurements. More importantly, SingMolT5 achieved high structural prediction accuracy, along with strong generalization to unseen structural variations not included in the training dataset. This work provides a proof-of-concept demonstration for a text-to-structure workflow in SME, serving as a foundational step toward integrating natural language models into future autonomous workflows for single-molecule research.

records.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

records.title: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity switches: Molecular design, pharmacology, and therapeutic considerations.
records.abstract: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems are chemogenetic tools that utilize small molecules to regulate protein association, higher-order assembly, and dissociation. Over the past three decades, an expanding repertoire of these systems has transformed the study of protein function and cellular signaling by enabling rapid, reversible, and tunable manipulation of protein localization, assembly, activity, and downstream physiological processes. As these technologies advance from experimental tools toward therapeutic applications, their translational potential depends not only on molecular switch performance but also on the properties of the chemical inducer and engineered protein components. In this review, we summarize the major classes and design principles of representative genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems, with particular emphasis on the pharmacological determinants that define their therapeutic operating window, including pharmacodynamic orthogonality, pharmacokinetics, tissue exposure, endogenous target engagement, and clinical readiness. We also examine how the biological origin and engineering of the chemogenetic modules influence immunogenicity and long-term compatibility. We further discuss exemplary applications, including pharmacological control of CAR-T cell activity, programmed cell death, CRISPR-based genome and epigenome engineering, and on-demand secretion of therapeutic proteins. Finally, we consider the delivery and coordinated expression of chemically regulated protein components as major remaining barriers to therapeutic implementation and highlight clinically compatible inducers, compact and minimally immunogenic protein modules, de novo protein design, and advances in viral and nonviral delivery as promising directions toward more reliable and pharmacologically tractable chemically controlled therapies.

records.title: Chemical Biology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Ligand Discovery to Virtual Cells.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

records.title: Extracellular Vesicle Derived Biomarkers for the Diagnosis of Neurodegenerative Diseases.
records.abstract: Liquid biopsy, a noninvasive method analyzing biofluids such as blood and cerebrospinal fluid, has transformed early detection and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) (30-150 nm) secreted by cells are pivotal because of their ability to cross the blood-brain barrier and carry disease-specific cargos like proteins and microRNAs. This review synthesizes recent advancements in EV-based liquid biopsy for diagnosing NDDs, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and frontotemporal dementia. Following PRISMA guidelines, we analyzed 113 studies from databases like PubMed and Scopus, highlighting EV-associated biomarkers' diagnostic potential. These vesicles offer a minimally invasive approach to detect proteinopathies and genetic markers, reflecting central nervous system pathology. Despite their promise, challenges such as standardized isolation protocols and clinical validation remain. This review discusses current trends, methodologies, and future directions for integrating EV-based diagnostics into clinical practice, emphasizing precision medicine for NDDs.

records.title: Bile-derived RNA N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation as a novel liquid biopsy biomarker for pancreatic cancer.
records.abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PCA) is a highly lethal malignancy with limited biomarkers for early diagnosis. Bile-derived epitranscriptomic biomarkers remain largely unexplored. We investigated whether bile-derived RNA N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation could serve as a diagnostic biomarker for PCA. Bile samples were collected from patients with PCA (n = 7), biliary tract cancer (BTC; n = 33), and common bile duct (CBD) stones (n = 10). Pancreatic juice samples from patients with pancreatic neoplastic lesions (PNLs; n = 2) and PCA (n = 5) were analyzed as an exploratory cohort. Global RNA m6A was quantified in duplicate using an ELISA-based colorimetric assay. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Bile-derived RNA m6A levels were higher in PCA than in the comparison groups. Bile-derived RNA m6A discriminated PCA from the combined BTC and CBD stone groups with an AUC of 0.993 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.970-1.000). The exploratory cut-off of 5.50% yielded 100.0% sensitivity and 97.7% specificity. In the exploratory pancreatic juice cohort, the AUC was 0.600 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.200-1.000), with a 4.16% cut-off, 60.0% sensitivity, and 100.0% specificity. Bile-derived global RNA m6A methylation was associated with PCA in this proof-of-concept cohort. The diagnostic performance and data-derived cut-off are preliminary and require validation in larger prospective independent multicenter cohorts before clinical application.

records.title: Continuous platelet enrichment from diluted blood using an acoustofluidic virtual filter.
records.abstract: Platelet enrichment is an important step in preparing blood samples for platelet analysis, motivating the development of continuous and controllable separation methods. Platelet analysis strongly depends on sample preparation. Conventional centrifugation-based platelet isolation requires repeated centrifugation and manual handling, while filter-based microfluidic technologies can suffer from clogging and mechanical stress that may cause platelet activation and sample loss. In this study, we developed an acoustofluidic chip for continuous platelet isolation and enrichment from diluted blood samples. Platelet-containing plasma is sequentially displaced toward the collection outlet through four serial lateral flow replacement units, while larger blood cells are confined to the central channel by a standing acoustic wave field that serves as a virtual filter. This design enables separation without membranes or obstructive filtration structures. In model-particle experiments conducted at a sample flow rate of 300 μL min-1, the recovery rate of 5 μm particles and the removal rate of 15 μm particles reached 90.34% and 94.02%, respectively. Platelet separation was further demonstrated using 10-fold diluted rat blood at a sample flow rate of 300 μL min-1, corresponding to a whole-blood-equivalent throughput of 30 μL min-1. The platelet-to-leukocyte ratio increased from 4.82 : 1 to 58.91 : 1 after separation. These results demonstrate continuous platelet enrichment relative to leukocytes, thus it is of potential to benefit the platelet-based liquid biopsy.

records.title: Donor-derived cell-free DNA levels predict 3-year outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable function.
records.abstract: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker for detecting acute rejection in kidney transplant recipients, but its prognostic value in patients with stable graft function remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between dd-cfDNA levels and long-term clinical outcomes. We retrospectively analyzed 267 kidney transplant recipients with stable renal function between January 2020 and July 2023, stratified by plasma dd-cfDNA levels into three groups: A (<1%, n = 205), B (1-<2%, n = 34), and C (≥2%, n = 28). Each patient contributed a single index dd-cfDNA measurement obtained during routine outpatient follow-up, which defined baseline; the interval from transplantation to the index measurement did not differ among groups (p = 0.124). Clinical outcomes included changes in serum creatinine, incidence of adverse events, graft loss, patient mortality, and biopsy findings over three years. Creatinine levels remained stable in Group A but increased significantly in Groups B and C from baseline to year 3 (1.38 to 1.96 mg/dL, p < 0.0001; and 1.36 to 1.84 mg/dL, p = 0.0019, respectively). Adverse events were significantly more frequent in Groups B (41.2%) and C (42.9%) compared with Group A (9.8%, p < 0.001). Graft loss rates were 0.98%, 11.76%, and 7.14% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (p = 0.002), and mortality showed a significant increasing trend across groups (p = 0.023). Elevated dd-cfDNA levels are associated with adverse long-term outcomes in kidney transplant recipients with stable graft function, suggesting that dd-cfDNA may serve as a valuable tool for early risk stratification and long-term monitoring in transplant care.

records.title: A miRpair-Based Molecular Comparator for Lung Cancer Diagnosis.
records.abstract: Early and precise cancer diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are promising diagnostic targets, but translating their complex, multi-dimensional expression signatures into clinical practice remains challenging. Here, we develop a concise molecular comparator using relative expression levels of specific miRNA pairs. The miRpair-based strategy demonstrates superior diagnostic performance compared to methods relying on the absolute quantification of single miRNAs. For non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnosis, we identify hsa-miR-148a-3p/hsa-miR-30d-5p as the optimal diagnostic pair from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.975. The silicon-based model achieves 90.3% accuracy in 93 clinical serum samples using quantitative analysis. We subsequently translate the comparator into a DNA-based molecular workflow via asymmetric polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and polymerase-assisted hybridization subtraction (PAH-Sub). This process performs threshold-based comparison of dual-miRNA relative abundance directly at the molecular level. Integration with catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) amplification generates fluorescent diagnostic outputs. Validation with 40 clinical serum samples yielded 87.5% accuracy, demonstrating the feasibility of molecular-level implementation of the miRpair decision rule. This study represents a proof-of-concept evaluation for NSCLC diagnosis. Further validation in independent cohorts incorporating clinically relevant disease controls will be required to establish broader clinical specificity.

records.title: Subtype-Specific Enrichment of HER2-Positive Extracellular Vesicles Enables Metabolomic Profiling for Breast Cancer Liquid Biopsy.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles have emerged as crucial components in the advancement of liquid biopsy. However, the efficient isolation of molecularly defined subpopulations remains challenging, limiting the performance of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based metabolomic analysis. In this study, HER2-targeting peptides were identified via phage display screening against the extracellular domain of HER2 and used to construct a peptide-directed magnetic separation platform (SA@HER2-2-MPMs) for the rapid and selective enrichment of HER2-positive extracellular vesicles. The biotinylated peptide enabled the specific recognition of HER2-enriched EVs' membranes, while streptavidin-functionalized magnetic polystyrene microspheres facilitated their efficient capture and magnetic separation. The enriched extracellular vesicles were subjected to subsequent metabolite extraction and LC-MS/MS analysis, forming the basis of an integrated workflow for subtype-specific extracellular vesicles isolation and metabolomic profiling. Compared with UC preparations, the peptide-directed workflow yielded lower measured concentrations of selected plasma-associated contaminants and supported downstream LC-MS/MS profiling. Metabolomic analysis revealed disease-associated alterations, and an exploratory predictive reanalysis using nested cross-validation and a held-out internal subset showed high within-cohort discrimination. This study establishes a peptide-directed strategy for isolating molecularly defined EV subpopulations and provides a platform for exploratory metabolic biomarker discovery in HER2-positive breast cancer; independent external validation remains required.
